review_notes: I read the target file and DilationPairCoordinates.lean, which defines scaledPairAssemble, scaledPairLayer and scaledPairLayerEquiv. I also checked the other uses (DilationPairFiltration, MultidegreeDilationPair). Those uses only wrap the equiv in definitions and don't use simp on it. The one issue is that the simp interface around scaledPairAssemble and scaledPairLayerEquiv is incomplete. I did not check whether the proposed simp lemmas fire as intended, since I can't run Lean. I found no cycle or competing-rule problems in the supplied file.

findings.problem: The two `simpa` calls in `hc` compute `(scaledPairLayerEquiv P Q hQP q (x, y)).val` by unfolding the definitions `scaledPairLayerEquiv` and `scaledPairAssemble` in the simp set. Neither has canonical simp lemmas. `scaledPairAssemble` has only `scaledPairDifference_assemble`, and `scaledPairLayerEquiv` has no apply lemma. So every consumer must unfold the implementation `(u + q • v, v)` and the structure `toFun`. The target then also needs `smul_eq_mul` and a hand-written `show` to match the unfolded form. This breaks the abstraction and makes the proof depend on how the definitions are written. The same would hold for any later proof that evaluates the equiv.
findings.proposed_change: In DilationPairCoordinates.lean, add `@[simp] theorem scaledPairAssemble_fst (q) (u v : L) : (scaledPairAssemble q u v).1 = u + q • v := rfl` and `@[simp] theorem scaledPairAssemble_snd ... .2 = v := rfl`. Also add `@[simp] theorem scaledPairLayerEquiv_apply_val (P Q hQP q) (x : Q × P) : ((scaledPairLayerEquiv P Q hQP q x : scaledPairLayer P Q q) : L × L) = (x.1 + q • x.2, x.2) := rfl`. Then the proofs of `hc` can use plain `simp [c, Basis.prod_apply]` without unfolding either definition, or `smul_eq_mul` needs only the reduced form. Keep the definitions semireducible or irreducible as desired.
findings.benefit: Callers get a stable normal form `(u + q • v, v)` through simp lemmas instead of unfolding definitions. The proof in this file becomes robust to changes in how `scaledPairAssemble` and `scaledPairLayerEquiv` are defined. Other uses of `dilationPairLayerEquiv`, which wraps this equiv, also get the evaluation lemma.

evidence.excerpt: def scaledPairAssemble (q : ℚ) (u v : L) : L × L := (u + q • v, v)
